stances.claim: Marcos has three major ICC options: (1) maintain the status quo and respect the July 18, 2023 Appeals Chamber 3-2 ruling without rejoining; (2) rejoin the ICC by unilateral recall of the withdrawal letter; or (3) cooperate without rejoining by opening executive-branch facilities to Karim Khan.

The ICC Appeals Chamber majority of three correctly concluded that PH had not shown 'genuine willingness or ability' to investigate especially the 'brains' -- but ignored the more fundamental issue of whether the petition was filed within the two-year reglementary period, simply claiming the PH had waived its right to pose it.

The vocal minority of two correctly insisted -- and CJ respectfully agrees -- that the ICC did not acquire jurisdiction because Bensouda filed the PTC petition on May 24, 2021 (granted Sept 15, 2021), both dates more than two years after PH withdrawal took effect on March 17, 2019; this jurisdictional vulnerability may explain why Khan has not publicly announced resumption.

Under Option 2, since the withdrawal was made solely by the President without Senate concurrence, the President may simply reverse his own act by recalling the letter of withdrawal -- no new Senate ratification needed, because the Aug 23, 2011 Senate Resolution No. 57 'still mightily stands to this day'; the Pangilinan v. Cayetano obiter dictum (penned by SAJ Leonen) backs this with logic, reason, and wisdom.

Option 3 -- opening NBI/PNP/DOJ to Khan while not rejoining -- is the diplomatically clever path, justifiable by 'the comity of nations and our abiding respect for the rule of law'; it can produce either of two seemingly disparate results: ICC concludes PH is genuinely willing and able, OR investigators rely on their own findings and 'ensnare the alleged perpetrators into the sticky ICC web.'

notable_anecdotes: The three-option analytical structure -- status quo / rejoin / cooperate-without-rejoining -- laid out as the canonical CJ decision-matrix for the Marcos administration.

The reglementary-period dissent -- Bensouda filed May 24, 2021 and PTC granted Sept 15, 2021, both dates more than two years after PH withdrawal effective March 17, 2019 -- with CJ noting that Khan's silence may itself signal awareness of the jurisdictional vulnerability.

The unilateral-recall doctrine -- 'the withdrawal was made solely by the President without the Senate's concurrence, [so] the President (regardless of who the incumbent is) may simply reverse his own act' -- paired with the observation that Senate Resolution No. 57 of Aug 23, 2011 ratifying the Rome Statute 'still mightily stands to this day.'

The Pangilinan v. Cayetano obiter dictum -- 'fittingly penned by Senior Associate Justice Marvic M.V.F. Leonen' -- backing the unilateral-recall logic 'with logic, reason, and wisdom,' even though obiter has only persuasive force.

Solicitor General Menardo Guevarra's status-quo summary -- Khan's investigators may enter and 'roam the countryside, observe their surroundings, listen to witnesses, receive documents, and see how free and capable our justice system is, with no cooperation from our government' -- capturing the awkward open-door-but-arms-folded posture.

The 'sticky ICC web' image -- Option 3's risk that investigators 'may decide to rely on their own findings and ensnare the alleged perpetrators' -- paired with the symmetric possibility that ICC concludes PH is genuinely able and willing.
VP Sara's 'though the heavens may fall' invocation -- adapting the Latin 'fiat justitia ruat caelum' to the case for showing local-institution viability.
Closing 'Abangan' -- CJ's canonical Tagalog wait-and-see closer signaling decision pending.

one_paragraph_summary: Following recent House hearings on whether the present regime should allow the ICC to investigate and prosecute alleged crimes against humanity during the Duterte administration, President Marcos said returning 'under the fold of the ICC' is 'under study... we'll just keep looking at our options.' Panganiban lays out three major options. First, MAINTAINING THE STATUS QUO -- not rejoining but respecting the July 18, 2023 ICC Appeals Chamber 3-2 ruling authorizing Karim Khan to resume his investigation of crimes from Nov 1, 2011 to March 16, 2019. The AC majority of three agreed PH had not shown genuine willingness or ability to investigate especially the 'brains,' but it ignored the more fundamental issue of whether the petition was filed within the two-year reglementary period, claiming PH had waived its right to raise it. The vocal minority of two (and CJ respectfully agrees) insisted the ICC did not acquire jurisdiction because Fatou Bensouda's PTC petition was filed May 24, 2021 and granted Sept 15, 2021 -- both more than two years after PH withdrawal took effect March 17, 2019. Khan's silence on resumption may reflect awareness of this vulnerability. SG Menardo Guevarra has summed up the PH stance: Khan's investigators may enter, roam the countryside, observe and listen, but no government cooperation. Second, REJOINING THE ICC -- since the withdrawal was made solely by the President without Senate concurrence, the President may unilaterally reverse the act by recalling the withdrawal letter; Senate Resolution No. 57 of Aug 23, 2011 ratifying the Rome Statute 'still mightily stands to this day' and needs no new ratification. The SC's Pangilinan v. Cayetano (March 16, 2021), fittingly penned by SAJ Leonen, backed this in an obiter dictum 'with logic, reason, and wisdom.' Third, COOPERATING WITHOUT REJOINING -- without recalling the withdrawal letter, the President can open NBI, PNP, and the DOJ Chief Prosecutor's Office to Khan via cabinet authorization, especially the secretary of justice; this can be justified by 'the comity of nations and our abiding respect for the rule of law.' Either of two seemingly disparate results would follow: the ICC concludes that PH is genuinely willing and able, or investigators rely on their own findings and 'ensnare the alleged perpetrators into the sticky ICC web.' VP Sara Duterte has formally asked the DOJ not to cooperate, supporting Option 1, upholding 'self-respect and dignity of our country' and demonstrating viability of local institutions 'though the heavens may fall.' Which option will the President take? Abangan.
